newsitem.title: INDIA: Reliance bonus cheers Bombay shrs, gains capped.
newsitem.headline: Reliance bonus cheers Bombay shrs, gains capped.

text.p: A generous bonus equity issue announced by a leading Indian private firm held the spotlight in resurgent Bombay shares on Thursday, brokers said.
Petrochemicals giant Reliance Industries Ltd ended weeks of feverish stock market guessing when it announced a one-for-one bonus share issue at a packed annual shareholders meeting.
"Much better than most had expected," said Alok Sethi, director at NatWest Markets.
Reliance share soared more than four percent on the news before closing at 377.50, up 11 rupees, after hitting 388 at the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).

"I think a liberal bonus was expected, but it'll still augur well for the market. Coupled with news of the cut in interest rates, the market should take it positively," said Brij Gopal Daga, chief general manager at Unit Trust of India.
The benchmark 30-share BSE index ended 17.43 points, or 0.43 percent, at a provisional 4,111.05.

India's central bank on Wednesday lowered its key bank rate to 10.0 percent from 11.0 and analysts said main state-run banks are more likely to opt for smaller cuts in prime rates, currently between 14.0 and 14.5 percent.
Bankers said they will consider cuts in prime rates over the coming days.
In market action, traders said share prices could be set for a period of consolidation in the short-run after strong buying support near the 4,000 level.

"The market is poised to rally 100 to 150 points," Sanjay Agarwal, chief executive of Lloyds Securities. "Its a buoyant market, there is institutional buying taking place, and there are no real negative factors."
"The market should not run away, we need a period of consolidation," added NatWest's Sethi.
